name: convert
title: Convert between currencies at the ECB rate
description: An amount converted between any two currencies the ECB lists, at its fixing in force on a day, computed exactly and rounded once. The euro to a currency is amount x rate, a currency to the euro is amount / rate, and two currencies go through the euro as amount x rate(to) / rate(from), both rates from the same fixing; no rate is rounded on the way. Answers the result with the rate or rates used and the fixing's date, and a sentence stating the rule, so the conversion can be quoted and checked. The ECB's rates are reference rates, not rates a bank or card will give.

amount.description: The amount, as a decimal string: "1250.50", "-75". Never a number.

from.description: The amount's currency, or EUR. ISO 4217; case ignored.

to.description: The currency wanted, or EUR. ISO 4217; case ignored.

date.description: The day of the conversion, YYYY-MM-DD in Frankfurt (an invoice's date, a payment's); default today.

rounding.description: How the result is rounded, once: half-up (halves away from zero, as invoices round) or half-even (banker's).

places.description: Digits after the point in the result.

result.description: The converted amount, computed exactly and rounded once

fixing_date.description: The date of the ECB fixing the conversion used

rate.description: The ECB's exact value, units of the currency per 1 EUR

rates.description: The rate of each non-euro currency in the conversion, units per 1 EUR, from the one fixing: one for a euro conversion, two for a cross rate

name: health
title: Health
description: Whether the ECB's reference rates can be read now: the date of its latest fixing and how many currencies it carries against the euro.

name: rate
title: ECB rate on a day
description: The European Central Bank's euro foreign exchange reference rate in force on a day: units of the currency per 1 EUR, as the exact value the ECB published (1 EUR = 1.1052 USD), with fixing_date, the date of the fixing it is. The ECB fixes rates on TARGET working days around 16:00 CET; a weekend, a TARGET holiday, or today before 16:00 CET takes the last working day's fixing, so the answer always says which one it used. Covers every day since 1999-01-04, including currencies the ECB has since dropped (HRK, RUB, BGN, ...) on the days it published them.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code: USD, GBP, JPY, CHF, ...; EUR where the tool allows it; case ignored.

date.description: The day, YYYY-MM-DD in Frankfurt; default today.

rate.description: The ECB's exact value, units of the currency per 1 EUR

fixing_date.description: The date of the ECB fixing this rate is

name: rates
title: ECB rates: every currency on a day, or a window
description: The ECB's reference rates as fixings, oldest first, each currency in units per 1 EUR as the ECB published it. With date (default today): every currency's rate in force that day, all from one fixing, whose date the answer gives. With from (and to, default today): every fixing the ECB published in the window, as many as fit in 2000 rates a call (a year of seven currencies, or all of them for about three months). Name currencies to narrow either; leave them out for all. Use it for a chart, an average or a check across several days.

currencies.description: ISO 4217 codes, e.g. ["USD", "GBP"], without EUR; default every currency the ECB published.

items.description: ISO 4217 code: USD, GBP, JPY, CHF, ...; EUR where the tool allows it; case ignored.

date.description: One day, YYYY-MM-DD in Frankfurt: the rates in force on it. Not with from.

from.description: A window's first day, YYYY-MM-DD: every fixing from it to `to`.

to.description: A window's last day, included; default today. Only with from.

date.description: The day asked for: fixings holds the one in force on it

fixing_date.description: With date: the date of the fixing that was in force

additionalProperties.description: The ECB's exact value, units of the currency per 1 EUR

rates.description: Units of each currency per 1 EUR on that fixing

fixings.description: Oldest first; a currency the ECB did not publish on a fixing is missing from that fixing's rates

count.description: How many rates the fixings hold

absent.description: Currencies asked for that the ECB published no rate of in the window
